findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the over-cap alert reaches `rebar-gerrit-alerts`: reuse autodeploy's existing countable-marker -> observability.sh -> CloudWatch-alarm path (naming the new token), or state the new direct `aws sns publish` call plus its aws-cli/IAM dependency and failure handling.
evidence: `search_files 'aws sns'` and `'aws sns publish'` return no matches across the repo
autodeploy.sh emits alerts exclusively via marker()/err() journald tokens (autodeploy.sh:176-177) that observability.sh converts to CloudWatch metrics — no direct SNS call exists
rebar-gerrit-alerts is a terraform SNS topic (monitoring.tf:37) currently fed by CloudWatch alarms, not by the script directly
findings.finding: The plan specifies an SNS alert via the `rebar-gerrit-alerts` topic but does not enumerate the mechanism by which autodeploy.sh would publish to SNS; the script has no SNS-publish path today (its alerting is the journald marker/token -> observability.sh -> CloudWatch pattern), so a new consumer/dependency is implied but unstated.
findings.location: Plan §Approach step 5 ('emit an SNS alert (the terraform `rebar-gerrit-alerts` topic)') and AC line 'an SNS alert is emitted (assert via `REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD`-style sink, no real SNS)'
scenarios: Implementer must decide whether the over-cap alert reuses the existing countable-marker path (alarmed via observability.sh/CloudWatch) or introduces a new direct `aws sns publish` call in the unattended root path — the latter adds an aws-cli/IAM dependency the plan never enumerates.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what re-drives MCP old-container retirement on ticks where `TARGET == DEPLOYED` (the script's early no-op exit at autodeploy.sh:306-311 currently returns before any retire logic) — e.g. run the still-serving/retire sweep on the no-op path (beside `reclaim_under_pressure`) so an idle-going old container is reclaimed promptly, not only on the next MCP source change.
evidence: Plan: 'Retire the old container off the critical path, gated by a flock-style "still serving?" check ... Retain the newest N; over a hard cap, emit an SNS alert ... rather than killing a live container or growing unbounded'
autodeploy.sh:306-311 `if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]; then rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"; reclaim_under_pressure; log "up to date"; exit 0; fi` — the no-op tick returns before any component delta is computed
ADR 0079 amendment: 'mirrors the immutable-release + retire-when-idle shape of the local ... updater' — but that updater's re-attempt cadence is not reproduced by autodeploy's early-exit oneshot
findings.finding: The plan adopts the local updater's 'retire-when-idle' shape but does not specify what re-triggers retirement of a still-serving old MCP container on a later tick; autodeploy.sh exits early on the up-to-date path before reaching any deploy/retire logic, so a deferred retirement is only re-attempted on the next MCP source change, not when the container goes idle.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (Retire the old container off the critical path) / autodeploy.sh lines 306-311 (up-to-date early exit)
scenarios: A shared MCP server stays busy (in_flight>0) through the deploy tick; the old container cannot be retired; on subsequent quiescent ticks TARGET==DEPLOYED so the retire check never runs; old containers pile up until the next real MCP source change trips the hard-cap SNS alert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define, for a shared `src/rebar/` change deploying both targets on one tick, how an mcp-target failure interacts with the single deployed-sha advance (autodeploy.sh:492) and SHA-keyed backoff (autodeploy.sh:314-328): state whether mcp failure blocks the sha advance (so both retry) or is isolated per-target, and how a partial (one-target-succeeded) tick avoids either abandoning the failed target or re-deploying the healthy one.
evidence: Plan: 'a shared `src/rebar/` change triggers BOTH targets — each is change-detected, drained, and deployed INDEPENDENTLY'

autodeploy.sh:492 `echo "$TARGET" > "$SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv ...` runs ONCE at the footer for all targets; OBS/CERTBOT failures are non-fatal and fall through to it, review-bot failure `exit 1`s before it
autodeploy.sh:314-328 BACKOFF_FILE is a single SHA-keyed record shared across the whole tick
findings.finding: For a shared `src/rebar/` change that triggers BOTH the review-bot and mcp targets, the plan does not specify the failure interaction with the single deployed-sha / SHA-keyed backoff: whether an mcp-branch failure is fatal (blocking the footer's sha advance) or non-fatal (falling through to advance deployed-sha), which determines whether a failed mcp deploy is ever retried.
findings.location: Change detection + blast radius ('each is change-detected, drained, and deployed INDEPENDENTLY') / autodeploy.sh lines 491-495 (single sha advance) + 320-328 (single backoff)
scenarios: review-bot deploys healthy, then the mcp build/health-check fails on the same tick: if mcp is non-fatal (OBS-style) the footer advances deployed-sha and the failed mcp deploy is never retried (silent stale MCP); if mcp is fatal (exit 1) the healthy review-bot is rebuilt again on every backoff retry of the shared SHA.

findings.finding: The plan claims the MCP retirement hard-cap and memory-pressure-abort conditions 'emit an SNS alert (the terraform rebar-gerrit-alerts topic)', but the on-box alerting architecture does not publish to SNS directly: existing autodeploy alerts emit a countable journal marker (marker()), which observability.sh greps via publish_autodeploy_marker_delta into a rebar/host CloudWatch custom metric, which a terraform aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) then routes to the rebar-gerrit-alerts topic. The plan names only the topic and omits the new marker token(s), the observability.sh grep/PutMetricData wiring, and the new CloudWatch alarm — so the alert as specified would not actually page, and the new infra is not fully reproducible-as-code for its own alarms.

findings.finding: The plan asserts autodeploy will directly 'emit an SNS alert (the terraform rebar-gerrit-alerts topic)' on the over-cap MCP-retirement path, but a direct SNS publish from the box is a NEW, unverified external integration: no `sns:Publish` IAM grant exists anywhere in the repo, and every existing autodeploy alert reaches SNS INDIRECTLY (journald `marker AUTODEPLOY_*` -> observability.sh CloudWatch metric delta -> terraform CloudWatch alarm with alarm_actions=[aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]).

findings.finding: The over-cap alert is specified as a new `REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD`-style sink (carried over from the local rebar-dev-update.sh prior art), but this box's autodeploy.sh already alerts exclusively via a countable `marker AUTODEPLOY_*` journal token -> observability.sh CloudWatch metric -> monitoring_autodeploy.tf CloudWatch alarm -> rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS topic; the script itself never publishes to SNS. Introducing a separate REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD sink duplicates that established alerting contract and adds a config surface for something the existing marker mechanism already captures.
scenarios: Retirement hard-cap is exceeded and the busy old container cannot be reclaimed: the plan would fire a REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD sink instead of emitting the existing marker token, so the alert would not flow through the box's real observability/CloudWatch/SNS path and would need a new terraform alarm or a direct-SNS credential.
A reviewer implements a direct `aws sns publish` from the script (per 'emit an SNS alert ... the terraform rebar-gerrit-alerts topic'), diverging from the script's no-direct-SNS design.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit `marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP <reason> <detail>` on the over-cap path (mirroring AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT), add the corresponding rebar/host metric in observability.sh and a CloudWatch alarm wired to aws_sns_topic.alerts in monitoring_autodeploy.tf, and change the AC oracle to assert the marker token is emitted (no new sink env var, no real SNS).
